Claude can use your Android phone now, and the app has been rebuilt from scratch.

**Phone control.** Pair an Android phone over wireless debugging and Claude can see its screen, tap, swipe, type and open apps on it, the same way it works on your desktop. While it works, a small overlay on the phone shows Claude's cursor and what it's doing, so you can watch or take over. Pairing is in the app under Phone: enter the code and address from the phone's Wireless debugging screen. Mirror opens the phone in scrcpy on your desktop.

**New app.** Every page was redrawn. The sidebar and toolbar are proper liquid glass that bends what scrolls under it, a step darker than the page in light mode and a step lighter in dark mode so labels stay easy to read. Settings are split into Computer, Phone, Assistant, Appearance and Keyboard instead of one long list, and the overview shows what Claude can reach right now.

**Shortcuts you can actually record.** The Keyboard page used to be a text box. Click a shortcut and press the keys: Hyprland's own binds are held off while it listens, so you can record combinations that are already in use.

**Fixes.** After a reload, Claude Code and the Claude app pick up new tools without a restart. Phone screenshots are about twice as fast as the first version.

Install `SudoClaude.flatpak` below over the old one:

```sh
flatpak install --user SudoClaude.flatpak
```
